answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 15 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the willow solution is checked at the quill gate and logged, the ferrous audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 38 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
